narrative: Your application was denied because the assessment placed your chance of bad credit at 25.0%, or about one in four. Although 25% may sound below half, the bank’s approval rule treats this level as too high for the loan requested. The three most influential factors in your assessment were your savings position, your property status, and your installment burden. Ranked first, your savings information—recorded as unknown or none—was the strongest factor, and it actually worked in your favor rather than against you. Ranked second, owning real estate also pushed your assessment toward lower risk. Ranked third, your installment rate of 1.00% of disposable income, compared with an approved-applicant average near 3%, reduced the estimated burden and again worked in your favor. Because all three top-ranked factors were protective, the denial was not caused by them; it reflects the remaining profile. In particular, your requested amount of 7,472 DM is well above the approved average of about 3,020 DM, and your employment status is unemployed. These less favorable details outweighed the positive top factors. Next, ask the lender for the specific decline reasons, review your credit report for errors, consider applying for a smaller amount, and provide stronger evidence of savings, stable employment, or a guarantor before reapplying.
